title: Ravioli with NS filling and tomato sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Ravioli are small pasta parcels traditionally made from thin wheat‑flour and egg dough. Inside is a filling of NS (natural raw blend), and the finished product is served with a tomato sauce that adds a bright aroma and gentle acidity.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ravioli originate from Italy, where they have been prepared for over a thousand years.
Tomato sauce code 3522 was specially formulated for ravioli to highlight the filling’s flavor.
The NS filling can include a mix of cheese, spinach and herbs, making it both nutritious and aromatic.
Traditionally, ravioli are boiled in salted water for 3–5 minutes before being tossed with sauce.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The NS filling provides high‑quality plant protein that supports muscle maintenance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tomato sauce and the raw blend supply vitamin B6 and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Lycopene
items.content: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that promotes heart health.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: When spinach is added to the filling, dietary fiber content increases, aiding digestion.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: The wheat‑flour dough can trigger allergic reactions in individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauce may be salty; those monitoring sodium intake should choose a reduced‑salt version.

items.title: Heat treatment
items.content: Undercooked ravioli may contain live bacteria from the filling, so proper cooking time is essential.

content.title: How to Serve
content.content: Boil the ravioli until al dente, drain, and toss with hot tomato sauce. Optionally garnish with grated Parmesan, fresh basil, or a drizzle of olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry ravioli in an airtight container in a cool, dry place for up to 6 months. Cooked ravioli and sauce keep in the refrigerator for no more than 3 days.
